verification: Read the recorded observation and test for each evaluation. Opened every linked image with an image decoder and parsed every linked JSON file. Many earlier cycles share a final screenshot gallery and QA record. Those artifacts corroborate the final run and do not independently reconstruct all rejected intermediate builds. Unnumbered follow-ups and review passes are not additional cycles.

The candidate restores the Explorer’s 4px sibling gap on the published template, rounds article images to 15px and sets inline TX-02 Regular to 80% of the surrounding font size with a 13px minimum at default zoom. Its tighter padding and normal line height let the surrounding paragraph set the line spacing.

The public site served `index-26310706.css`. The previous local design served `index-9c9c1bbf.css`. On the same Azure Machine Configuration article, the public site rendered inline code at 15px on phones and 16px on desktop, in weight 500. The actual syntax characters inside the code box rendered at 14px and weight 400. A fresh request in all three engines returned the older published style. Expanded Explorer siblings also had a 0px top margin on that public build, compared with 4px locally. [Published site](https://husenjan.com/)

The site owner found the previous 12.5–13px inline size too small after finding the earlier 15–16px published style too large. The revised style uses the existing `--code-size` token for inline TX‑02 and fenced syntax. Both measure **14px at a 16px browser default**. The new size applies to regular, bold and table code. The [SCSS rule](quartz/styles/custom.scss) changes one property. [Type scale](DESIGN_SYSTEM.md)

The site-wide checks uncovered a second issue in the Blog listing. A browser-enforced **20px minimum font size** enlarged the date text even when the nominal CSS font and grid units stayed the same. At 900px in Chrome, Brave and Edge, the first date needed 18.84px more space than its 112px track allowed. Date ink extended beyond the row, and the document became 902px wide. The same defect existed before the inline size change.
